history.content: How can hot, dry, windy weather affect wildfire behaviour?

Authority: General background. Answer: Hot weather dries out vegetation and soils, making fuels easier to ignite and allowing fires to burn more intensely. Dry conditions reduce fuel moisture, so flames can spread faster and embers can ignite additional areas more readily. Wind supplies oxygen, pushes flames and heat into unburned vegetation, and can carry embers ahead of the main fire, causing rapid or unpredictable spread. Limitations: General background — not verified against the FireLens corpus.
